name: keltner_channel_trend_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when the index sustains above its 5-minute Keltner Channel upper band (EMA(60) + 2×ATR(60)) for 3 consecutive 5-second bars, it signals institutional directional flow has overwhelmed the volatility-adjusted supply ceiling — the band is harder to breach than Bollinger Bands because ATR widens in choppy conditions, so a sustained breach specifically means price velocity exceeds current micro-volatility regime, not just a single-bar noise spike. TWAP/VWAP algorithms filling large directional orders continue pushing for 30-90 seconds as only 40-60% of institutional orders are typically filled at the breakout bar. The ADX(36) filter confirms that +DI and -DI have diverged meaningfully over the past 3 minutes, validating that the breakout is driven by directional flow rather than a two-sided auction spike.

indicators.name: kc_mid
indicators.purpose: 5-minute EMA as Keltner midline. Compressed from original's 20-min (EMA(20) on 1-min) to 5-min because we are catching the fast breakout continuation, not the multi-hour trend. At 5s bars, a 20-minute EMA (EMA(240)) would react too slowly to the intraday momentum pulses that drive 30-120s trades. 5-min EMA (EMA(60)) is the minimum meaningful trend baseline that filters tick noise while still being responsive to intraday shifts.

indicators.name: atr_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute ATR for channel width calibration. Matches kc_mid period for consistency. At 5s bars, ATR(60) captures the current session volatility regime (last 5 minutes) without being dominated by a single spike bar. This ensures the channel width reflects genuine micro-volatility, making channel breaches meaningful.

indicators.name: kc_upper
indicators.purpose: Keltner upper band. Multiplier of 2x matches original. A breach signals price is moving faster than 2x the 5-minute ATR-calibrated volatility — genuine momentum rather than noise. The ATR-normalized band means this signal is more reliable in both high and low volatility regimes compared to standard deviation bands.

indicators.name: kc_lower
indicators.purpose: Keltner lower band for bearish breakout detection. Symmetric to kc_upper.

indicators.name: adx_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute ADX for trend strength confirmation. Original used ADX(14) on 1-min bars (= 14 min). Compressed to ADX(36) = 3 min because we need near-term trend confirmation for a 30-120s trade — a 14-minute ADX would confirm trends far too slowly and would frequently lag by the time the channel break occurs. 3 minutes gives enough +DI/-DI divergence history to distinguish directional flow from two-sided auction without being so fast it generates noise.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.purpose: Session VWAP as directional bias filter. No scaling needed — cumulative measure. Channel breakout above VWAP confirms institutional accumulation alignment; below VWAP confirms distribution. Replaces original's volume filter (volume > SMA_vol(20)) since index volume at 5s is noisy.

conditions: close > kc_upper for 3 consecutive 5s bars (15s persistence filter)
close > vwap (above session VWAP confirms accumulation bias)
buy_ce.confirmation: 3-bar persistence (15 seconds) filters single-bar spikes — same number of bars as original (3 consecutive 1-min bars), same time logic applied at 5s frequency

conditions: close < kc_lower for 3 consecutive 5s bars (15s persistence filter)
close < vwap (below session VWAP confirms distribution bias)
buy_pe.confirmation: 3-bar persistence to confirm sustained breakdown below lower channel

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option pts (~8 spot pts at delta 0.5). NIFTY Keltner Channel width at typical ATR is 10-20 spot pts. If a genuine breakout fails and price re-enters the channel by 4 option pts, the institutional flow that created the breakout has definitively reversed. Calibrated to 1-minute NIFTY move magnitude (3-7 pts) — a loss within that range means the thesis is wrong, cut before a full reversal consumes more premium.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option pts (~14 spot pts). Genuine Keltner breakouts with ADX confirmation on NIFTY typically extend 15-25 spot pts beyond the channel as TWAP/VWAP algo orders continue filling. 7 pts captures approximately 50-60% of the median first continuation leg (1:1.75 R:R). Stopping at 7 avoids giving back gains as the institutional order fills and momentum fades.

filters.vix_filter: VIX between 12-28: channel breakouts become unreliable below VIX 12 (no volatility, channel collapses) or above 28 (gap risk overwhelms channel logic)
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST: skip first 15 minutes of opening noise where channels have not yet calibrated to session volatility
filters.volume_filter: none (index volume at 5s is noisy; VWAP alignment and ADX provide directional confirmation instead)
filters.trend_filter: ADX(36) > adx_threshold (22 default) confirms directional flow before entry; close vs VWAP gives macro bias
filters.spread_filter: N/A (limit order execution at candle close)

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — trend following on NIFTY index is structurally robust (institutional TWAP/VWAP flow is persistent), but ADX at 3-min lookback lags; may confirm trends only after 30-40% of the move is already done

adaptation_notes: Original was equity spot on NIFTY100 FnO stocks at 1-min bars, holding 30-180 minutes. Core Keltner Channel trend-following idea transfers cleanly to NIFTY index: channel breakout = genuine directional force exceeding ATR-calibrated volatility. Key adaptations: (1) Lookback compressed from 20-min EMA/ATR to 5-min (EMA(60)/ATR(60)) — we catch the fast 30-120s continuation burst, not the multi-hour trend; (2) ADX compressed from 14-min to 3-min (ADX(36)) for faster trend confirmation at 5s resolution; (3) Volume filter (volume > SMA_vol(20)) replaced by VWAP alignment — volume is noisy on index at 5s while VWAP provides cleaner directional bias; (4) Session start shifted to 09:30 (570 min) to skip 15 minutes of opening auction noise where channels are uncalibrated; (5) Hold time compressed from 30-180 min to 30-120s (24 bars max). Differentiated from existing keltner_channel_reversion_v1 (EMA(24), reversion on channel touch, 30-90s hold) by: opposite thesis (trend continuation vs mean reversion), longer lookback (60 vs 24), ADX filter (trend vs no trend filter), and VWAP directional bias.
weaknesses: ADX(36) at 3-minute lookback lags sharply — entry confirmed only after 30-40% of momentum move is already done, reducing effective capture
3-bar persistence (15s) may miss fast breakouts in low-ATR environments where channel is tight and price moves through quickly
NIFTY genuine Keltner breakouts with ADX > 22 occur only 1-3 times per session, limiting trade frequency to below max_trades_per_day most days

Differentiated from keltner_channel_reversion_v1 but both share EMA+ATR channel logic — on range days both strategies may trade at the same bars (one sees a reversion signal, this one sees a failed breakout) creating correlated losses
